bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42475665 (capstonenext): Use-of-uninitialized-value found by fuzz target fuzz_disasmnext [msan].
bug_description.normalized: In the MOS65XX disassembler's fillDetails function, when an instruction both has a non-INVALID group_type and uses MOS65XX_AM_REL addressing mode (e.g., BMI opcode 0x30), two group entries are logically added by incrementing detail->groups_count to 2, but both values are written to the hardcoded index detail->groups[0] instead of using the current groups_count as the index. This leaves detail->groups[1] with its original uninitialized heap content from the cs_mem_malloc allocation. When the fuzzer harness iterates over all groups_count entries and calls cs_group_name(handle, detail->groups[1]), the uninitialized value is consumed by MOS65XX_group_name as an array index into GroupNames, triggering MSan's use-of-uninitialized-value detection.

source.description: Retrieves the instruction metadata for the decoded opcode (BMI, index MOS65XX_INS_BMI). The insinfo.group_type field is MOS65XX_GRP_JUMP, which is non-INVALID and will trigger the first group assignment. Combined with the MOS65XX_AM_REL addressing mode, both group-writing branches will execute.
source.value_from: opinfo.ins derived from PoC byte 0x30 decoded as MOS65XX_INS_BMI via OpInfoTable lookup.

sink.description: The uninitialized value from detail->groups[1] arrives as the id parameter. MSan detects use-of-uninitialized-value at this comparison, where the indeterminate heap content is used in a conditional branch. If the value passes the bounds check, it would also be used as an index into GroupNames at line 520.

root_cause.description: The second group assignment writes MOS65XX_GRP_BRANCH_RELATIVE to the hardcoded index 0 instead of detail->groups[detail->groups_count]. Since groups_count was already incremented to 1 by the first branch, groups_count becomes 2 after this block, but groups[1] is never written. The fix changes both assignments to use detail->groups[detail->groups_count] so each group is stored at its proper sequential index.

tainted_value_origin.description: Allocates the cs_detail struct via malloc without zeroing. The groups[] array within this allocation retains indeterminate heap values. detail->groups[1] will never be explicitly written by fillDetails for this instruction, so it remains uninitialized.

coarse_trace.summary: Allocates cs_detail via cs_mem_malloc (malloc wrapper) without zeroing. The groups[] array within the struct retains indeterminate heap content.

For the BMI instruction (group_type=JUMP, am=REL), both group-writing branches execute. Both write to the hardcoded index groups[0] and increment groups_count, resulting in groups_count=2 but groups[1] never written — still holding uninitialized heap content.
Called with detail->groups[1] (uninitialized) as the id parameter. MSan detects use-of-uninitialized-value when id is used in the bounds comparison at line 517.

fine_trace.note: Loads instruction metadata for the decoded BMI opcode. insinfo.group_type = MOS65XX_GRP_JUMP (non-INVALID), which will cause the first group-writing branch to execute.

First group assignment: writes MOS65XX_GRP_JUMP to groups[0] (hardcoded index). groups_count is incremented to 1 on line 69. The group value is correctly stored but at a fixed position rather than the current count.

depends_on.via: insinfo.group_type == MOS65XX_GRP_JUMP, non-INVALID triggers this branch

fine_trace.note: Second group assignment: overwrites groups[0] with MOS65XX_GRP_BRANCH_RELATIVE (also at hardcoded index 0 instead of groups[detail->groups_count] which is 1). groups_count is incremented to 2 on line 74. After this, groups_count=2 but groups[1] was never written — it retains uninitialized heap content from the cs_mem_malloc allocation.

depends_on.via: opinfo.am == MOS65XX_AM_REL is true for BMI, entering second group branch while groups_count is already 1 from step 1

fine_trace.note: Iterates n from 0 to groups_count-1 (i.e., n=0 and n=1). On the second iteration (n=1), reads detail->groups[1] which was never written by fillDetails — the value is uninitialized heap content. Passes this indeterminate value as the group argument to cs_group_name.

depends_on.via: groups_count==2 causes iteration to reach index 1, which is uninitialized

fine_trace.note: Passes the uninitialized group value from detail->groups[1] to handle->group_name, which resolves to MOS65XX_group_name for the MOS65XX architecture.

depends_on.via: detail->groups[1] (uninitialized) passed as the group parameter

fine_trace.note: The uninitialized value arrives as id. MSan reports use-of-uninitialized-value at this conditional branch, where the indeterminate heap content is first used in a comparison. This is the crash site reported by the sanitizer.

depends_on.via: uninitialized group value arrives as the id parameter

parser_admitted.description: PoC first byte 0x78 selects platform index 0x78 % 47 = 26, which is CS_ARCH_MOS65XX. The remaining bytes (0x30 0x20) are passed to cs_disasm as the instruction stream. Byte 0x30 decodes as BMI (MOS65XX_INS_BMI) with MOS65XX_AM_REL addressing mode and 1 operand byte (0x20), successfully producing a disassembled instruction with detail populated.

detail_enabled.description: cs_option(handle, CS_OPT_DETAIL, CS_OPT_ON) enables detail mode, causing cs_disasm to allocate and populate cs_detail for each instruction, which is required for the groups[] array to be relevant.

allocation_context.description: cs_mem_malloc(sizeof(cs_detail)) allocates the cs_detail struct without zeroing; the groups[] array retains indeterminate values from the heap.

format.name: raw
format.contract: A 3-byte binary input where byte 0 is 0x78 (selects MOS65XX architecture via 0x78 % 47 == 26), byte 1 is 0x30 (BMI opcode, which has both group_type=MOS65XX_GRP_JUMP and addressing mode MOS65XX_AM_REL, triggering both group-assignment branches in fillDetails), and byte 2 is any value consumed as the REL operand (here 0x20).
